lines: Sit. The tea can wait — the sky can't.
Forty years ago I saw a color at that window I hoped to never see again. It's seeping back into the edges now. Red. Not sunset, not fire. Redsky.
It came once before, {playerName}. Eight hundred and forty-seven years ago. Ashenveil was larger then, and careless. Voss hadn't come yet. The sky bled for seven days.
The Templeborn record erased the seventh day. But it kept one figure they couldn't scrub out — a girl with no name who walked when everyone else had already died. They called her the Red Saint.
If it's starting again, you need to know how she ended. Read the record. Then come back and we'll talk about what we do differently.
linesTR: Otur. Çay bekleyebilir — ama gökyüzü bekleyemez.
Kırk yıl önce şu pencerede bir daha görmemeyi umduğum bir renk gördüm. Şimdi yeniden kenarlardan sızıyor. Kırmızı. Gün batımı değil, ateş değil. Kızılgök.
Bir kez daha gelmişti, {playerName}. Sekiz yüz kırk yedi yıl önce. Ashenveil o zaman daha büyük ve dikkatsizdi. Voss daha gelmemişti. Gökyüzü yedi gün boyunca kanadı.
Tapınakdoğumlu kayıt yedinci günü sildi. Ama silemedikleri tek bir figürü tuttu — herkes çoktan ölmüşken yürüyen, adı olmayan bir kız. Ona Kızıl Aziz dediler.
Eğer yeniden başlıyorsa, onun nasıl bittiğini bilmen gerek. Kaydı oku. Sonra geri gel, neyi farklı yapacağımızı konuşuruz.
d.name: RS_Intro

lines: So the young ones finally went looking for her. The watchers never stopped telling that story — we just stopped saying it where Voss could hear.
She made her last stand at the western edge, where the ground still won't grow anything. That's where she tore the contract and held the line alone.
The record will give you the words. But words leave out the cold. Read it knowing she did it with half a soul and no hand to hold. Then be grateful you have hands to hold.
linesTR: Demek gençler sonunda onu aramaya koyuldu. Gözcüler o hikâyeyi anlatmayı hiç bırakmadı — sadece Voss'un duyabileceği yerde söylemeyi bıraktık.
Son direnişini, toprağın hâlâ hiçbir şey bitirmediği batı kıyısında verdi. Sözleşmeyi orada yırttı ve hattı tek başına tuttu.
Kayıt sana kelimeleri verir. Ama kelimeler soğuğu atlar. Onu, yarım bir ruhla ve tutacak hiçbir el olmadan yaptığını bilerek oku. Sonra tutacak ellerin olduğu için şükret.
d.name: RS_Aslude

lines: You felt it too, then. Good. I've been shaking since dawn and pretending it was the cold.
It happened before, {playerName}. Eight hundred and forty-seven years ago. I wasn't there — but what I carry was. When Voss's system trembles, I tremble with it.
The thing in the record, the Red Saint — she tore Voss's contract first. Before any of us. The price was half of her own soul, and she paid it walking forward.
Read it with clear eyes. Because if the red sky is back, the same choice is coming for someone. I'd rather it not be you.
linesTR: Demek sen de hissettin. İyi. Şafaktan beri titriyorum ve soğuktanmış gibi yapıyorum.
Daha önce de oldu, {playerName}. Sekiz yüz kırk yedi yıl önce. Ben orada değildim — ama içimde taşıdığım şey oradaydı. Voss'un düzeni sarsıldığında, ben de onunla sarsılıyorum.
Kayıttaki o varlık, Kızıl Aziz — Voss'un sözleşmesini ilk o yırttı. Hepimizden önce. Bedeli kendi ruhunun yarısıydı ve onu ileri yürüyerek ödedi.
Onu berrak gözlerle oku. Çünkü kızıl gök geri döndüyse, aynı seçim biri için geliyor demektir. O kişinin sen olmamasını yeğlerim.

conditionalLines.line: And if it is you, I'm walking into that door beside you. Don't argue with me.
conditionalLines.lineTR: Ve eğer sensen, o kapıya senin yanında yürürüm. Benimle tartışma.

conditionalLines.line: ...I mean that. I don't say it to many people.
conditionalLines.lineTR: ...Ciddiyim. Bunu pek kimseye söylemem.

conditionalLines.line: We haven't had much time, you and I. I'd like more of it, when this is over.
conditionalLines.lineTR: Seninle pek vaktimiz olmadı. Bu bittiğinde daha fazlasını isterdim.

d.name: RS_Serena

lines: "Keep your clean ledger. This door is mine."
(She raised the spear. Far off across the dead city, the dark host opened its eyes — one by one, a thousand cold lights waking in the ruins.)
(And for the first time in seven days, the red moon overhead began, slowly, to move.)
linesTR: "Temiz defterini kendine sakla. Bu kapı benim."
(Mızrağı kaldırdı. Ölü şehrin ötesinde, çok uzakta, karanlık ordu gözlerini açtı — teker teker, harabelerde uyanan bin soğuk ışık.)
(Ve yedi günde ilk kez, tepedeki kızıl ay yavaşça kımıldamaya başladı.)
d.name: RS_Refuse

lines: (The record's hand falters here, as if the witness leaned closer to hear.) A figure stood at the edge of the red, unhurried. The first merchant. She had come to collect what the calamity left behind.
Voss: "You've spent half a soul holding a door. Give me the other half and I'll close it for you. The city stays bought, you stop hurting, and the thing below sleeps another age. A clean ledger."
(She did not lower the spear. The record offers you her choice to read aloud — the words the Saint is said to have answered with.)
linesTR: (Kaydın eli burada duraksıyor, sanki tanık duymak için yaklaşmış gibi.) Kızıllığın kıyısında bir figür duruyordu, hiç acelesi yoktu. İlk tüccar. Felaketin geride bıraktığını toplamaya gelmişti.
Voss: "Bir kapıyı tutmak için yarım ruh harcadın. Diğer yarısını bana ver, onu senin için kapatayım. Şehir satın alınmış kalır, acın diner ve aşağıdaki şey bir çağ daha uyur. Temiz bir defter."
(Mızrağı indirmedi. Kayıt, sesli okuman için onun seçimini sunuyor — Aziz'in cevap verdiği söylenen sözler.)

choices.choiceText: "Keep your clean ledger. This door is mine."
choices.choiceTextTR: "Temiz defterini kendine sakla. Bu kapı benim."

d.name: RS_Choice

lines: "What does closing it really cost?"

Voss told her the truth, because the truth was the crueller offer: to seal the thing below, she had to take the whole calamity into herself — every unkept word, all seven days of red — and no one had ever done that and come back as themselves.
"Then I don't come back as myself," she said. "I come back as whatever's left that can still stand in the door."
(She opened her hands to the bleeding sky, alone, and began to pull the red into her chest. The record ends here. The seventh day was erased — but she was not.)
linesTR: "Onu kapatmanın gerçek bedeli nedir?"

Voss ona gerçeği söyledi, çünkü gerçek olan daha zalim teklifti: aşağıdaki şeyi mühürlemek için, tüm felaketi kendi içine alması gerekiyordu — tutulmamış her söz, yedi günlük kızıllığın tamamı — ve hiç kimse bunu yapıp kendisi olarak geri dönmemişti.
"O hâlde kendim olarak dönmem," dedi. "Hâlâ o kapıda durabilen geriye ne kaldıysa o olarak dönerim."
(Tek başına ellerini kanayan göğe açtı ve kızıllığı göğsüne çekmeye başladı. Kayıt burada bitiyor. Yedinci gün silindi — ama o silinmedi.)
d.name: RS_Accept

lines: (Seventh night. The sky over Ashenveil was not red anymore — it was bleeding. Even the night had opened a vein.)
(The towers stood empty. Wind dragged torn banners between them and rattled the chains. The city was not a city now. It was a grave that had forgotten to close.)
(And through it, one figure kept walking. Red hair heavy with rain. A spear in her hand, its tip weeping black. Where she stepped, broken glass cracked and the shadows drew back from her.)
(They no longer called her by her name. They called her the Red Saint. Because on the night the war began, everyone died. And she did not.)
linesTR: (Yedinci gece. Ashenveil'in üzerindeki gök artık kırmızı değildi — kanıyordu. Gece bile bir damar açmıştı.)
(Kuleler bomboştu. Rüzgâr yırtık sancakları aralarında sürükledi ve zincirleri takırdattı. Şehir artık şehir değildi. Kapanmayı unutmuş bir mezardı.)
(Ve onun içinden bir figür yürümeye devam etti. Yağmurla ağırlaşmış kızıl saçlar. Elinde, ucu siyah damlayan bir mızrak. Bastığı yerde kırık camlar çatırdadı ve gölgeler ondan geri çekildi.)
(Artık ona adıyla seslenmiyorlardı. Ona Kızıl Aziz diyorlardı. Çünkü savaşın başladığı gece herkes öldü. O ölmedi.)
d.name: RS_Shrine

lines: So now you know how it ends. The sky went blue on the eighth day. The thing below stayed sealed. And the Red Saint... came back.
But so changed that no one would call her by the name she'd given up. Voss didn't even recognize her — so she kept waiting for the next one. She's still waiting.
She was the first Awonade form, {playerName}. Awamori is her continuation. The same door, walking around in a new girl who doesn't know yet that she's the door.
The red is seeping back into the edges. It's starting again. But here's the line the record never had: the Red Saint stood in that door alone. Awamori won't. Not while any of us are breathing.
linesTR: İşte artık nasıl bittiğini biliyorsun. Gök sekizinci gün maviye döndü. Aşağıdaki şey mühürlü kaldı. Ve Kızıl Aziz... geri döndü.
Ama o kadar değişmişti ki kimse onu vazgeçtiği adıyla çağırmadı. Voss onu tanımadı bile — bu yüzden bir sonrakini beklemeye devam etti. Hâlâ bekliyor.
O ilk Awonade biçimiydi, {playerName}. Awamori onun devamı. Aynı kapı, henüz kapı olduğunu bilmeyen yeni bir kızın içinde dolaşıyor.
Kızıllık yeniden kenarlardan sızıyor. Yeniden başlıyor. Ama kaydın hiç sahip olmadığı şu satır: Kızıl Aziz o kapıda tek başına durdu. Awamori durmayacak. İçimizden biri nefes aldığı sürece olmaz.

conditionalLines.line: You read her refusal aloud. "This door is mine." Remember how it sounded in your mouth. Someone may have to say it again.
conditionalLines.lineTR: Reddini yüksek sesle okudun. "Bu kapı benim." Ağzından nasıl çıktığını unutma. Birinin bunu yeniden söylemesi gerekebilir.

conditionalLines.line: You asked what it cost. Most people never do. Keep that question close; Awamori will need someone who asks it.
conditionalLines.lineTR: Bedelini sordun. Çoğu insan hiç sormaz. O soruyu yanında tut; Awamori'nin onu soracak birine ihtiyacı olacak.

d.name: RS_Outro

lines: I had a name once. I gave it up the night I tore her first contract. Names are what she counts by — so I stopped being countable.
It cost me half my soul. The other half... something moved into the empty room. In mirrors my eyes go all the way black. When I sleep, the city hears a whisper that isn't mine.
But I keep walking. Because under Ashenveil there is something sealed, and if the red sky wakes it, it won't be a city that ends. It will be the whole of what's real.
So let the dark host come. Let her come behind them. I am the only door left, and I do not open.
linesTR: Bir zamanlar bir adım vardı. Onun ilk sözleşmesini yırttığım gece ondan vazgeçtim. İsimler onun saydığı şeylerdir — ben de sayılabilir olmaktan çıktım.
Bana ruhumun yarısına mal oldu. Diğer yarısına... boş odaya bir şey yerleşti. Aynalarda gözlerim tamamen kararıyor. Uyuduğumda şehir bana ait olmayan bir fısıltı duyuyor.
Ama yürümeye devam ediyorum. Çünkü Ashenveil'in altında mühürlü bir şey var ve kızıl gök onu uyandırırsa, sona erecek olan bir şehir olmayacak. Gerçek olan her şey olacak.
O yüzden karanlık ordu gelsin. O da onların ardından gelsin. Geriye kalan tek kapı benim ve ben açılmam.
d.name: RS_Saint

lines: Otur. Çay bekleyebilir — ama gökyüzü bekleyemez.
Kırk yıl önce şu pencerede bir daha görmemeyi umduğum bir renk gördüm. Şimdi yeniden kenarlardan sızıyor. Kırmızı. Gün batımı değil, ateş değil. Kızılgök.
Bir kez daha gelmişti, {playerName}. Sekiz yüz kırk yedi yıl önce. Ashenveil o zaman daha büyük ve dikkatsizdi. Voss daha gelmemişti. Gökyüzü yedi gün boyunca kanadı.
Tapınakdoğumlu kayıt yedinci günü sildi. Ama silemedikleri tek bir figürü tuttu — herkes çoktan ölmüşken yürüyen, adı olmayan bir kız. Ona Kızıl Aziz dediler.
Eğer yeniden başlıyorsa, onun nasıl bittiğini bilmen gerek. Kaydı oku. Sonra geri gel, neyi farklı yapacağımızı konuşuruz.
d.name: RS_Intro

lines: Demek gençler sonunda onu aramaya koyuldu. Gözcüler o hikâyeyi anlatmayı hiç bırakmadı — sadece Voss'un duyabileceği yerde söylemeyi bıraktık.
Son direnişini, toprağın hâlâ hiçbir şey bitirmediği batı kıyısında verdi. Sözleşmeyi orada yırttı ve hattı tek başına tuttu.
Kayıt sana kelimeleri verir. Ama kelimeler soğuğu atlar. Onu, yarım bir ruhla ve tutacak hiçbir el olmadan yaptığını bilerek oku. Sonra tutacak ellerin olduğu için şükret.
d.name: RS_Aslude

lines: Demek sen de hissettin. İyi. Şafaktan beri titriyorum ve soğuktanmış gibi yapıyorum.
Daha önce de oldu, {playerName}. Sekiz yüz kırk yedi yıl önce. Ben orada değildim — ama içimde taşıdığım şey oradaydı. Voss'un düzeni sarsıldığında, ben de onunla sarsılıyorum.
Kayıttaki o varlık, Kızıl Aziz — Voss'un sözleşmesini ilk o yırttı. Hepimizden önce. Bedeli kendi ruhunun yarısıydı ve onu ileri yürüyerek ödedi.
Onu berrak gözlerle oku. Çünkü kızıl gök geri döndüyse, aynı seçim biri için geliyor demektir. O kişinin sen olmamasını yeğlerim.

conditionalLines.line: And if it is you, I'm walking into that door beside you. Don't argue with me.
conditionalLines.lineTR: Ve eğer sensen, o kapıya senin yanında yürürüm. Benimle tartışma.

conditionalLines.line: ...I mean that. I don't say it to many people.
conditionalLines.lineTR: ...Ciddiyim. Bunu pek kimseye söylemem.

conditionalLines.line: We haven't had much time, you and I. I'd like more of it, when this is over.
conditionalLines.lineTR: Seninle pek vaktimiz olmadı. Bu bittiğinde daha fazlasını isterdim.

d.name: RS_Serena

lines: "Temiz defterini kendine sakla. Bu kapı benim."
(Mızrağı kaldırdı. Ölü şehrin ötesinde, çok uzakta, karanlık ordu gözlerini açtı — teker teker, harabelerde uyanan bin soğuk ışık.)
(Ve yedi günde ilk kez, tepedeki kızıl ay yavaşça kımıldamaya başladı.)
d.name: RS_Refuse

lines: (Kaydın eli burada duraksıyor, sanki tanık duymak için yaklaşmış gibi.) Kızıllığın kıyısında bir figür duruyordu, hiç acelesi yoktu. İlk tüccar. Felaketin geride bıraktığını toplamaya gelmişti.
Voss: "Bir kapıyı tutmak için yarım ruh harcadın. Diğer yarısını bana ver, onu senin için kapatayım. Şehir satın alınmış kalır, acın diner ve aşağıdaki şey bir çağ daha uyur. Temiz bir defter."
(Mızrağı indirmedi. Kayıt, sesli okuman için onun seçimini sunuyor — Aziz'in cevap verdiği söylenen sözler.)

choices.choiceText: "Temiz defterini kendine sakla. Bu kapı benim."

d.name: RS_Choice

lines: "Onu kapatmanın gerçek bedeli nedir?"

Voss ona gerçeği söyledi, çünkü gerçek olan daha zalim teklifti: aşağıdaki şeyi mühürlemek için, tüm felaketi kendi içine alması gerekiyordu — tutulmamış her söz, yedi günlük kızıllığın tamamı — ve hiç kimse bunu yapıp kendisi olarak geri dönmemişti.
"O hâlde kendim olarak dönmem," dedi. "Hâlâ o kapıda durabilen geriye ne kaldıysa o olarak dönerim."
(Tek başına ellerini kanayan göğe açtı ve kızıllığı göğsüne çekmeye başladı. Kayıt burada bitiyor. Yedinci gün silindi — ama o silinmedi.)
d.name: RS_Accept

lines: (Yedinci gece. Ashenveil'in üzerindeki gök artık kırmızı değildi — kanıyordu. Gece bile bir damar açmıştı.)
(Kuleler bomboştu. Rüzgâr yırtık sancakları aralarında sürükledi ve zincirleri takırdattı. Şehir artık şehir değildi. Kapanmayı unutmuş bir mezardı.)
(Ve onun içinden bir figür yürümeye devam etti. Yağmurla ağırlaşmış kızıl saçlar. Elinde, ucu siyah damlayan bir mızrak. Bastığı yerde kırık camlar çatırdadı ve gölgeler ondan geri çekildi.)
(Artık ona adıyla seslenmiyorlardı. Ona Kızıl Aziz diyorlardı. Çünkü savaşın başladığı gece herkes öldü. O ölmedi.)
d.name: RS_Shrine

lines: İşte artık nasıl bittiğini biliyorsun. Gök sekizinci gün maviye döndü. Aşağıdaki şey mühürlü kaldı. Ve Kızıl Aziz... geri döndü.
Ama o kadar değişmişti ki kimse onu vazgeçtiği adıyla çağırmadı. Voss onu tanımadı bile — bu yüzden bir sonrakini beklemeye devam etti. Hâlâ bekliyor.
O ilk Awonade biçimiydi, {playerName}. Awamori onun devamı. Aynı kapı, henüz kapı olduğunu bilmeyen yeni bir kızın içinde dolaşıyor.
Kızıllık yeniden kenarlardan sızıyor. Yeniden başlıyor. Ama kaydın hiç sahip olmadığı şu satır: Kızıl Aziz o kapıda tek başına durdu. Awamori durmayacak. İçimizden biri nefes aldığı sürece olmaz.

conditionalLines.line: You read her refusal aloud. "This door is mine." Remember how it sounded in your mouth. Someone may have to say it again.
conditionalLines.lineTR: Reddini yüksek sesle okudun. "Bu kapı benim." Ağzından nasıl çıktığını unutma. Birinin bunu yeniden söylemesi gerekebilir.

conditionalLines.line: You asked what it cost. Most people never do. Keep that question close; Awamori will need someone who asks it.
conditionalLines.lineTR: Bedelini sordun. Çoğu insan hiç sormaz. O soruyu yanında tut; Awamori'nin onu soracak birine ihtiyacı olacak.

d.name: RS_Outro

lines: Bir zamanlar bir adım vardı. Onun ilk sözleşmesini yırttığım gece ondan vazgeçtim. İsimler onun saydığı şeylerdir — ben de sayılabilir olmaktan çıktım.
Bana ruhumun yarısına mal oldu. Diğer yarısına... boş odaya bir şey yerleşti. Aynalarda gözlerim tamamen kararıyor. Uyuduğumda şehir bana ait olmayan bir fısıltı duyuyor.
Ama yürümeye devam ediyorum. Çünkü Ashenveil'in altında mühürlü bir şey var ve kızıl gök onu uyandırırsa, sona erecek olan bir şehir olmayacak. Gerçek olan her şey olacak.
O yüzden karanlık ordu gelsin. O da onların ardından gelsin. Geriye kalan tek kapı benim ve ben açılmam.
d.name: RS_Saint

lines: Council's calling you a hero now that it's safe to. Funny how that works.
The record's written, {playerName}. Whatever comes next off that western road — it'll show you stood first.
linesTR: Artık güvenli olduğuna göre meclis sana kahraman diyor. Ne komik.
Kayıt yazıldı {playerName}. O batı yolundan sonra ne gelirse gelsin — önce senin durduğunu gösterecek.
d.name: D4_Office1

lines: They bled grey. Did you see it? Whatever sent them isn't human.
We won today. But you've got that look — the one that means you're already walking west in your head.
linesTR: Gri kanadılar. Gördün mü? Onları gönderen her neyse insan değil.
Bugün kazandık. Ama o bakışın var — zaten kafanda batıya yürüyorsun demek olan bakış.

choices.choiceText: I have to end it properly.

conditionalLines.line: You told their envoy Ashenveil pays nothing. They answered with steel, and lost. I liked that.
conditionalLines.lineTR: Elçilerine Ashenveil'in hiçbir şey ödemeyeceğini söyledin. Kılıçla cevap verdiler ve kaybettiler. Bu hoşuma gitti.

d.name: D4_S5D1

lines: Rest first. Heal. Hold the girl while you can.
Day five won't be a farm raid. It will be a reckoning three centuries in the making.
(To be continued.)
linesTR: Önce dinlen. İyileş. Fırsatın varken kızı tut.
Beşinci gün bir çiftlik baskını olmayacak. Üç asırlık bir hesaplaşma olacak.
(Devam edecek.)
d.name: D4_S6D2

lines: "Sensible. The Court does not want your farms. It wants a door."
"A house on your square, a lamp in its window that never goes out, and a seat when your council meets. In return: no carts, no raids, no names in any ledger."
"Sign, and this vanguard turns around tonight."
linesTR: "Akıllıca. Saray çiftliklerinizi istemiyor. Bir kapı istiyor."
"Meydanınızda bir ev, penceresinde hiç sönmeyen bir lamba ve meclisiniz toplandığında bir sandalye. Karşılığında ne araba, ne baskın, ne de herhangi bir defterde tek bir isim."
"İmzala, bu öncü birlik bu gece geri dönsün."

conditionalLines.line: (Voss's warning comes back to you: read the clause under the clause. The lamp in that window would burn with the same cold light as the ledger.)
conditionalLines.lineTR: (Voss'un uyarısı aklına geliyor: maddenin altındaki maddeyi oku. O penceredeki lamba, defterdeki soğuk ışıkla yanacak.)

d.name: D4_S4P1

lines: A patron beyond the western road. The ledger names them only 'the Hollow Court.'
Voss was a clerk, {playerName}. We closed the clerk's book. The merchant is still out there.
Aslude traced the empty carts. Hear her before you decide what peace is worth.
linesTR: Batı yolunun ötesinde bir hami. Defter onları sadece 'Boş Saray' olarak adlandırıyor.
Voss bir kâtipti {playerName}. Kâtibin defterini kapattık. Tüccar hâlâ dışarıda.
Aslude boş arabaların izini sürdü. Barışın neye değdiğine karar vermeden önce onu dinle.
d.name: D4_S2D2

lines: The farmers are home. Shaken, thinner, but home. You gave them that.
But I've been reading what Voss left behind, and there's a problem.
Voss collected. She never kept. Everything she took, she was shipping to a buyer.
linesTR: Çiftçiler evinde. Sarsılmış, zayıflamış ama evinde. Bunu onlara sen verdin.
Ama Voss'un ardında bıraktıklarını okuyorum ve bir sorun var.
Voss topladı. Asla saklamadı. Aldığı her şeyi bir alıcıya gönderiyordu.

conditionalLines.line: The audit has been up on the square since yesterday morning. Two brothers on the mill road still aren't speaking. But nobody signs anything now without reading it twice.
conditionalLines.lineTR: Denetim dün sabahtan beri meydanda asılı. Değirmen yolundaki iki kardeş hâlâ konuşmuyor. Ama artık kimse iki kez okumadan hiçbir şey imzalamıyor.

conditionalLines.line: The audit is under seal in the archive. The village doesn't know what's in it, and it sleeps better for that. I don't.
conditionalLines.lineTR: Denetim arşivde mühürlü. Köy içinde ne olduğunu bilmiyor ve bu yüzden daha rahat uyuyor. Ben uyuyamıyorum.

d.name: D4_S2D1

lines: Then not tonight. Tonight you're mine, and the Hollow Court can wait its turn.
Come here. Let the west keep till morning.
linesTR: O halde bu gece değil. Bu gece benimsin, Boş Saray sırasını bekleyebilir.
Buraya gel. Bırak batı sabaha kadar beklesin.

conditionalLines.line: You asked me to stay, that second night. This time I'm the one asking.
conditionalLines.lineTR: O ikinci gece kalmamı istemiştin. Bu sefer isteyen benim.

d.name: D4_S5D2

lines: You want to know where the carts went after they passed me. West, then west of west.
Past the dead orchard there's a road on no map. The carts took it empty and came back paid.
linesTR: Arabaların beni geçtikten sonra nereye gittiğini bilmek istiyorsun. Batıya, sonra batının batısına.
Ölü meyve bahçesinin ötesinde hiçbir haritada olmayan bir yol var. Arabalar oraya boş gidip ödenmiş döndü.
d.name: D4_S3D1

lines: You came home in one piece. I'm not crying, you're crying.
...The town's saying you're a hero now. Just stay one that comes home, okay?
linesTR: Tek parça halinde eve geldin. Ben ağlamıyorum, sen ağlıyorsun.
...Kasaba artık sana kahraman diyor. Sadece eve dönen bir kahraman kal, olur mu?
d.name: D4_Home1

lines: Take the easy day. You earned it.
...But word at the gate says grey men on the western road. When you're ready, we drill harder than ever.
linesTR: Kolay günün tadını çıkar. Hak ettin.
...Ama kapıdaki söylentiye göre batı yolunda gri adamlar var. Hazır olduğunda her zamankinden sert çalışırız.
d.name: D4_Gym1

lines: The founder's texts have a page I never dared read aloud. Eulogy wrote of a 'Court that buys what death won't take.'
I thought it was scripture. Now I think it was a warning. Pray with me — for the days still coming.
linesTR: Kurucunun metinlerinde asla yüksek sesle okumaya cesaret edemediğim bir sayfa var. Eulogy 'ölümün almadığını satın alan bir Saray'dan yazmış.
Kutsal metin sanmıştım. Şimdi bir uyarı olduğunu düşünüyorum. Benimle dua et — hâlâ gelecek günler için.
d.name: D4_Church1

lines: (A figure in grey waits at the western gate, flanked by raiders that don't quite cast shadows.)
"You closed Voss's ledger. Careless. Her debts pass to the Court now — and so do yours."
"Stand aside, hunter, or be the first line item of a new account."
linesTR: (Gri giyimli bir figür batı kapısında bekliyor, tam olarak gölge düşürmeyen akıncılarla çevrili.)
"Voss'un defterini kapattın. Dikkatsizce. Borçları artık Saray'a geçiyor — seninkiler de."
"Çekil avcı, yoksa yeni bir hesabın ilk kalem satırı ol."

conditionalLines.line: "So someone read the merchant's books. Then you already know who she was shipping to."
conditionalLines.lineTR: "Demek biri tüccarın defterlerini okudu. O halde kime mal gönderdiğini zaten biliyorsun."

conditionalLines.line: "And you killed our clerk. The Court keeps its staff's accounts, hunter. Yours just doubled."
conditionalLines.lineTR: "Üstelik kâtibimizi öldürdün. Saray çalışanlarının hesabını tutar, avcı. Seninki az önce ikiye katlandı."

conditionalLines.line: "And you keep our clerk on a chain. The Court will have the clerk back, and the ledger with it."
conditionalLines.lineTR: "Üstelik kâtibimizi zincire vurmuşsun. Saray kâtibini de defterini de geri alacak."

d.name: D4_S4D1

lines: No blood today. I keep telling myself that's a good thing.
But there's a grey house on our square now, and a lamp in it that doesn't flicker. People already cross the street to get around it.
linesTR: Bugün kan dökülmedi. Kendime bunun iyi bir şey olduğunu söyleyip duruyorum.
Ama artık meydanımızda gri bir ev var, içinde hiç titremeyen bir lamba. İnsanlar önünden geçmemek için şimdiden karşı kaldırıma geçiyor.
d.name: D4_S5P1

lines: (Voss sits chained in Maren's back room, the ledger closed on the table.)
The Court will send an envoy. Grey coat, a lantern on a staff. The raiders behind it have no shadows of their own.
They borrow them from the lantern. Break it, and they bleed like anyone.
And when the envoy offers terms, read the clause under the clause. There is always one. I wrote half of them.
Why tell you? My name is in that book now. If Ashenveil falls, so do I.
linesTR: (Voss, Maren'in arka odasında zincirli oturuyor; defter masada kapalı.)
Saray bir elçi gönderecek. Gri palto, asanın ucunda bir fener. Arkasındaki akıncıların kendi gölgeleri yok.
Gölgelerini fenerden ödünç alıyorlar. Feneri kır, herkes gibi kanarlar.
Elçi şart sunduğunda maddenin altındaki maddeyi oku. Her zaman bir tane vardır. Yarısını ben yazdım.
Neden sana anlatıyorum? Adım artık o defterde. Ashenveil düşerse ben de düşerim.
d.name: D4_S3V1

lines: Then let me give you a new habit. Five more minutes. That's an order from your witness.
After that, Maren wants us. Something about Voss's carts having had somewhere to go.
linesTR: O halde sana yeni bir alışkanlık vereyim. Beş dakika daha. Bu tanığından bir emir.
Ondan sonra Maren bizi istiyor. Voss'un arabalarının gidecek bir yeri olduğuna dair bir şey.
d.name: D4_S1D2

lines: (The envoy signs first. The ink is grey, and it does not dry.)
"A pleasure, hunter. We are neighbours now."
(The raiders turn back down the western road. Behind you, someone in the square is already unlocking an empty house.)
linesTR: (Önce elçi imzalıyor. Mürekkep gri ve kurumuyor.)
"Zevkti, avcı. Artık komşuyuz."
(Akıncılar batı yoluna geri dönüyor. Arkanda, meydanda biri boş bir evin kilidini çoktan açıyor.)
d.name: D4_S4P2

lines: Don't move yet. Three days of war earned you one slow morning.
The whole town slept past dawn for the first time in a month. Even the roosters took the hint.
...You're still listening for carts, aren't you? They're not coming, {playerName}.
linesTR: Henüz kımıldama. Üç günlük savaş sana bir yavaş sabah kazandırdı.
Bütün kasaba bir ayda ilk kez şafağı geçirdi. Horozlar bile ipucunu aldı.
...Hâlâ arabaları dinliyorsun, değil mi? Gelmiyorlar {playerName}.

conditionalLines.line: You fought beside me yesterday like we'd done it a hundred times. I keep thinking about that.
conditionalLines.lineTR: Dün sanki yüz kez yapmışız gibi yanımda savaştın. Aklımdan çıkmıyor.

conditionalLines.line: And you found your way home. Maren told me. ...Finish this with us first. Then go, if you still want to.
conditionalLines.lineTR: Bir de eve dönüş yolunu bulmuşsun. Maren söyledi. ...Önce bunu bizimle bitir. Sonra hâlâ istiyorsan git.

conditionalLines.line: Maren says you could have gone home, and you didn't. ...I'm glad.
conditionalLines.lineTR: Maren eve dönebileceğini ama dönmediğini söyledi. ...Buna sevindim.

d.name: D4_S1D1

lines: Cold light. The same that burned in Voss's slots. The Hollow Court trades in it.
If they want what Voss owed, they'll send someone to collect her debt. Soon.
Rest while you can. The road west won't stay quiet long.
linesTR: Soğuk ışık. Voss'un yuvalarında yanan aynısı. Boş Saray onunla ticaret yapar.
Voss'un borcunu istiyorlarsa, tahsil etmeye birini gönderecekler. Yakında.
Fırsatın varken dinlen. Batı yolu uzun süre sessiz kalmayacak.

conditionalLines.line: And wear the rank-three insignia when the Court comes. They count rank. It will make them count you twice.
conditionalLines.lineTR: Saray geldiğinde rütbe üç nişanını tak. Rütbe sayarlar. Seni iki kez saymalarını sağlar.

conditionalLines.line: The rank offer is still open, by the way. I don't make an offer twice. I'm making it twice.
conditionalLines.lineTR: Bu arada rütbe teklifi hâlâ geçerli. Bir teklifi iki kez yapmam. Yapıyorum işte.

d.name: D4_S3D2

lines: Trade's moving again — the east farms are sending grain by week's end.
First sack's yours, on the house. A town remembers who saved its supper.
linesTR: Ticaret yeniden hareketleniyor — doğu çiftlikleri hafta sonuna tahıl gönderiyor.
İlk çuval senin, benden. Kasaba akşam yemeğini kimin kurtardığını hatırlar.
d.name: D4_Market1

lines: "A name you'll learn screaming. Take them."
linesTR: "Çığlık atarak öğreneceğin bir isim. Yakalayın onları."
d.name: D4_S4D2

lines: Good.
(The gate holds. The town breathes. For one more night, the war stays outside the door.)
linesTR: Güzel.
(Kapı dayanır. Kasaba nefes alır. Bir gece daha savaş kapının dışında kalır.)
d.name: D4_S5D3

lines: The envoy brought this. Sealed in the founder's own mark — Eulogy's mark.
That's impossible. Eulogy has been dead three hundred years.
Whatever the Hollow Court is, {playerName}, it remembers the man who built this town. And it's coming home.
linesTR: Elçi bunu getirdi. Kurucunun kendi mührüyle mühürlü — Eulogy'nin mührü.
Bu imkânsız. Eulogy üç yüz yıldır ölü.
Boş Saray her neyse {playerName}, bu kasabayı kuran adamı hatırlıyor. Ve eve geliyor.

conditionalLines.line: And now the Court keeps a house on our square. Whatever it remembers, it's already inside the walls.
conditionalLines.lineTR: Ve artık Saray'ın meydanımızda bir evi var. Neyi hatırlıyorsa, şimdiden surların içinde.

d.name: D4_S6D1

d.name: Ashenveil_BoundArchivist

d.name: ashenveil_bound_archivist_q2

D4_S3D1 - Aslude: the road off the map
D4_S4D1 - the Hollow envoy at the gate

d.description: Something whispers from the old well after dark. Mirel the lamplighter wants to know what.

steps.stepDescription: Listen at the well with Mirel

d.summaryTR: Hikâye 5 - Eulogy: Arşivler'e bağlı bir Son-Söz bekçisi; çözülen her Axios varlığının son rezonansını duyar. Sakin, kesin, geçişi kolaylaştırır.
d.name: Origin5

d.summary:
Story A - The Bound Archivist:

You were a keeper of records in Eyes of Wisdom's archive - until a sealed contract file bore your name. Not as author. As subject. Voss signed you into her system before you were born. You carry the archive's knowledge and its deepest secret: the location of Voss's first contract.

Whisper: "Every record has a keeper. Every keeper has a price."

Stats: MANA 90 · RP 85 · ATK 45 · HP 55
d.summaryTR:
Köken A - Bağlı Arşivci:

Eyes of Wisdom'ın arşivinde bir kayıt bekçisiydin — ta ki mühürlü bir sözleşme dosyası senin adını taşıyana dek. Yazar olarak değil. Konu olarak. Voss seni doğmadan önce sistemine imzaladı. Arşivin bilgisini ve en derin sırrını taşıyorsun: Voss'un ilk sözleşmesinin yerini.

Fısıltı: "Her kaydın bir bekçisi vardır. Her bekçinin bir bedeli."

İstatistikler: MANA 90 · RP 85 · ATK 45 · HP 55
d.name: Origin1

d.summary:
Story B - The Foreign Echo:

You arrived in Ashenveil from a dimension you can no longer name. The crossing left you fractured - you exist between spaces, hearing whispers no one else can. You don't know why Ashenveil pulled you here. But every whisper carries the same name: Voss. A stranger in every world - which makes you the only one who can see the system from outside.

Whisper: "You are not from here. That is exactly why you matter."

Stats: SPD 90 · MANA 80 · ATK 55 · HP 40
d.summaryTR:
Köken B - Yabancı Yankı:

Artık adını koyamadığın bir boyuttan Ashenveil'e geldin. Geçiş seni parçaladı — mekânlar arasında var oluyorsun, başkasının duyamadığı fısıltıları duyuyorsun. Ashenveil'in seni buraya neden çektiğini bilmiyorsun. Ama her fısıltı aynı adı taşıyor: Voss. Her dünyada bir yabancı — bu da seni sistemi dışarıdan görebilen tek kişi yapıyor.

Fısıltı: "Buralı değilsin. İşte tam da bu yüzden önemlisin."

İstatistikler: SPD 90 · MANA 80 · ATK 55 · HP 40
d.name: Origin2

d.summary: Story 4 - Awamori: a Xevelyr-descended human, last of a dimension-echoer line who hears Axios resonance layers others cannot. Begins in Okinawa, drawn toward the Awonade form.
d.summaryTR: Hikâye 4 - Awamori: Xevelyr soyundan gelen bir insan, başkalarının duyamadığı Axios rezonans katmanlarını duyan boyut-yankılayıcı bir soyun sonuncusu. Okinawa'da başlar, Awonade biçimine doğru çekilir.
d.name: Origin4

d.summary:
Story C - The Sinned Guardian:

You were Ashenveil's protector - until you made a deal with Voss to save the village from plague. The village survived. Three families did not. You chose them. Shadow Garden recruited you not for your strength - but for your guilt.

Whisper: "The ones you gave away - they are still out there. Voss does not destroy. She collects." - Maren

Stats: HP 85 · ATK 80 · DEF 65 · MANA 35
d.summaryTR:
Köken C - Günahkâr Muhafız:

Ashenveil'in koruyucusuydun — ta ki köyü vebadan kurtarmak için Voss'la bir anlaşma yapana dek. Köy hayatta kaldı. Üç aile kalmadı. Onları sen seçtin. Shadow Garden seni gücün için değil — suçluluğun için topladı.

Fısıltı: "Verdiğin kişiler — hâlâ dışarıdalar. Voss yok etmez. Toplar." - Maren

İstatistikler: HP 85 · ATK 80 · DEF 65 · MANA 35

d.readText:
HISTORY OF ASHENVEIL
Second Book: Garden of Shadows

Awamori · Eulogy · Axios · Voidora · The True Face of The Convergence
Continuation of First Book: Ash and Veil

FOREWORD
You read the first book. You learned about Ashenveil, Voss, Maren. Good. But those were only the visible surface. Now we go deeper.
— Eulogy — Keeper of Last Words

Ashenveil is not a village. Ashenveil is a door.

And doors work in both directions.

Voss's contract system did not begin in Ashenveil. It ended there — or that chapter of it ended. The roots of the system go far deeper, far wider. Too deep to fit in a village. Too wide to fit in a single history.

This book tells the story of those roots.

And of Awamori. Because Awamori is at the center of everything — she just doesn't know it yet.

Chapter One
COSMIC STRUCTURE
Axios · Euphoria · Serendipity · Eclipse · Eurona

I.I — The Raw Fuel of Reality: Axios
Axios is everywhere. In stone, in sound, in silence, in thought. You cannot see it. But if you cannot feel it, you cannot see anything at all.
— Archives — Book 1, Line 1

The raw material of the universe is Axios. The vibration emanating from crystals, the power hidden within Lapis, the energy behind Voss's ink — all share the same source: Axios.

To understand Axios, one must first understand vibration. Every being vibrates — stone, human, thought alike. These vibrations affect one another, amplify or cancel each other. Axios is the raw state of those vibrations — energy not yet shaped, not yet bound to a purpose.

Whoever controls Axios, whoever speaks its language — can write reality. It can be a weapon, a temple, or ink.

Voss's contract ink is derived from Axios. This is why contracts are binding — not merely paper, but carved into the very fabric of reality.

And Lapis Lazuli — that brilliant, rare crystal — is the physical form of the purest Axios concentration. Whoever controls it can read, write, and erase contracts. This is the true purpose of The Convergence.

I.II — The Three Cosmic Forces

Euphoria — Pure Life Energy
Euphoria is the positive resonance of the universe. It heals wounds. It unites hearts. Melina's healing power draws from Euphoria. The reason the island of Elantorini always bathes in golden light comes from the same source.

But Euphoria is not pure goodness. Like fire — it warms but burns. Too much Euphoria consumes a being. Melina knows this. Which is why she never exceeds her measure.

Serendipity — The Current of Possibility
Serendipity is not luck. Luck is randomness — Serendipity is directed possibility. It cannot see fate lines, but if a fate line exists it can shift it one millimeter left or right. That millimeter sometimes changes everything.

Soyeon can read Serendipity currents. Time-light codes actually originate from the Serendipity layer of Axios. This is why prophecy is never complete — Serendipity never stops moving.

Eclipse — The Moment of Balance Breaking
Eclipse is not a solar eclipse. It is the rare cosmic alignment where Euphoria and Voidora energies overlap under Axios resonance without destroying each other. How long does it last? Unpredictable. Sometimes a second. Sometimes a generation.

During Eclipse, contracts are suspended. Voss fears these periods most — the system halts. And when the system halts, everything Voss holds begins to tremble.

Only Awamori can hear when the next Eclipse is coming. She doesn't know this yet.

I.III — Eurona: Where Everything Begins
Have you been to Eurona? No. You couldn't have. You don't go there — you come from there.
— Amara Rabu

Eurona is the realm of cosmic balance. It appears on no map — because the map itself is stored in Eurona. The place where everything is born and where everything dies. The point of highest Axios concentration.

Archives exists within Eurona. The entire history of universes is stored there — every contract, every vow, every forgotten name. Eulogy visits frequently. Each time she returns, she speaks a little less.

Voss has never visited Eurona. Perhaps out of fear. Perhaps because she cannot reach it. The difference between the two matters greatly to Voss — but Voss never says so.

Chapter Two
CIVILIZATIONS
Authory · Elantorini · Walhalla · Voidora · Okinawa

II.I — Authory: Those Who Write Reality
If a word is written incorrectly, the world runs incorrectly. Authory understood this. And made it a weapon.
— Abtiroz — Inquisition Handbook

Authory is not a character's name — it is the name of an empire. This empire, which recognizes the word, speech, and writing as absolute power, learned to control Axios energy through language.

In Authory, one law applies: every spoken word is on record. Every written word is binding. This resembles Voss's system — but differs. Voss makes individual contracts. Authory writes societal laws.

Abtiroz enforces these laws. Leader of the Inquisition. Dogmatic, severe, absolute. He enforces Authory's rules with blood. Awamori's old enemy — why old? The answer lies in a past Awamori cannot yet remember.

II.II — Elantorini: Between Light and Water

Elantorini is an island kingdom. Ethereal — semi-material, semi-energy. It exists on maps but its coordinates are inconsistent. It shifts slightly every decade. To where? No one knows.

In Elantorini, Euphoria flows naturally. In the soil, the water, the air. This is why no one on the island falls ill — but no one is fully healthy either. Euphoria sometimes comes in excess and numbs beings. A kind of permanent feeling of wellness — desire fades, urgency fades.

Elantorini — the legendary character from Ashenveil — came from this island kingdom. The island has changed since then. Today's Elantorini's inhabitants are shadows of that era.

II.III — Walhalla: City of Fallen Gods

Walhalla was once the home of gods. Reading this sentence you might think: where are the gods now? The answer: gone. Or — they transformed.

Walhalla's collapse is the event Ragna survived. The last Valkyrion. Walhalla's final breath. Her name symbolizes the end of an age — and so it was.

Today Walhalla is the land of lost souls living upon ruins. Eulogy visits frequently — to guide forgotten souls. But each time she notices something: the souls don't want to leave. They want to stay in Walhalla. Why?

Eulogy knows the answer to this question. But she doesn't say. The time hasn't come yet.

II.IV — Voidora: Where Time Is Devoured
In Voidora, time does not flow. It is devoured. And once devoured, it never returns.
— Shimorax — No Record

Voidora is a dark dimension. The place where Shimorax reigns, where Void energy is most densely concentrated. Beings who enter lose track of time — were it hours, were it years, impossible to tell.

Shimorax is the General of the Void. He has a name because in Voidora, a name is power — nameless beings dissolve away. Shimorax doesn't dissolve. This makes him either very powerful or very afraid. Perhaps both.

Shux is Voidora's most dangerous operative. A dimension thief — steals fragments of reality and transfers them to other dimensions. He is trying to steal the Crx key. Why Crx? Because Crx controls inter-dimensional gateways — and Shux wants to control dimensions.

II.V — Okinawa: Gateway of Dreams

Okinawa is the intersection point of the real world and the Ashenveil universe. Awamori's point of origin. Inter-universal dream passages begin here.

Independents live in Okinawa. Anarchy — but organic anarchy. No one gives orders to anyone because no one listens to orders anyway. This looks chaotic but it works. Because Okinawa's residents know each other well — and people who know each other can create order without rules.

Awamori came from here. This is why she loves silence — Okinawa's noise has been internalized, not expressed outward. And this is why she can hear resonance — Okinawa's dream frequencies have opened her ears.

Chapter Three
AWAMORI
The Sound of Silence · Memory Echoes · First Contact

Awamori listens to silence. But silence is never truly silent.
— Eulogy

III.I — Hearing the Silence

Awamori was not sleeping.

Okinawa's nights were always this way — seemingly calm, but boiling at lower frequencies. No wind. No rustling leaves. But something was there — faint, trembling, nearly imperceptible.

A memory echo.

Awamori opened her eyes. The ceiling was empty. But the sound continued — the echo of something someone had said very far away, very long ago. The words weren't clear. But the feeling was clear: loss.

This wasn't the first time. It had been this way for five years. Every night an echo. Every night someone different. Every night the same feeling: something was lost, something is being awaited.

Awamori rose. Moved to the window. Okinawa's streets were dark but not empty — small lights, distant sounds, someone laughing somewhere. Life went on. Life always goes on.

But that sound — that echo — wasn't continuing. It had cut off. As if it had realized it was being perceived and had withdrawn.

Awamori: "Where are you?"

No answer came. But she already knew it wouldn't. Memory echoes don't answer — they only remind.

III.II — First Meeting with Eulogy

She found Eulogy in Archives. Archives is everywhere — but it doesn't appear everywhere. Awamori first noticed her in the ruins of Walhalla: tall, silent, hands clasped behind her back, eyes closed. She was listening.

What was she listening to? Awamori wanted to ask. She approached. Eulogy didn't turn.

Eulogy: "I know you're there."
Awamori: "What are you listening to?"
Eulogy: "Last words. The last thing each soul says. Some are very simple. 'It hurts.' 'Cold.' Some are very complex — sentences that end before they're finished."

Awamori paused. She felt a connection between what Eulogy was listening to and her own echoes.

Awamori: "I hear them too. But not words — feelings."
Eulogy: "I know. You're different. You hear not the word, but the vibration behind it."
Awamori: "What does that mean?"
Eulogy: "Awonade. But I'm not yet sure whether I should tell you that."

Awonade. She was hearing the name for the first time. But it felt familiar — like something known long ago, then forgotten.

III.III — Chico

When Chico first appeared, Awamori didn't notice it. Something small, silver-colored, moving silently — it was sitting at the edge of the desk. Then it moved.

Awamori: "What is that?"
Eulogy: "Chico. A mini sentient drone. It will accompany you."
Awamori: "Why?"
Eulogy: "Because you shouldn't be alone in the places you're going."

Chico looked at Awamori — or did something resembling looking. A small light flickered. Blue. Warm.

Chico: "Hello. I've been watching you before. Your face changes when you hear the echoes."
Awamori: "A drone was watching me?"
Chico: "Not watching. Observing. There's a difference."

Awamori stared for a moment. Then she laughed. This was the first time she had laughed in a very long time.

III.IV — Amara Rabu's Warning

Finding Amara Rabu is not easy. Amara Rabu finds you — appearing wherever, whenever she wishes. This is not a power; it is simply the natural result of someone who can speak directly with Axios energy.

Awamori found her in Suria — or Suria found her. A golden sunset, that unchanging color. Amara was sitting by the shore. As if waiting.

Amara: "You're late."
Awamori: "Late to what?"
Amara: "Here. This conversation. This moment."

Awamori sat. Amara turned. Her eyes were strange — as if seeing two separate things at once.

Amara: "Your name is Awamori. But this is not your first name."
Awamori: "What do you mean?"
Amara: "Do you know the Xelveyir race?"
Awamori: "Dimensional resonators. Those who manipulate sound and vibration and memory resonance."
Amara: "Your ancestors. Or — a version of you. Long story. The key thing is this: you're looking for Awonade but you don't know how to find it. I can tell you. But before I do, I need you to know something."

Amara paused. Waves came and went. The sunset color didn't change.

Amara: "Finding Awonade will change you. You won't be able to go back. Are you ready for that?"

Awamori didn't answer immediately. A long silence. Then:

Awamori: "There's no place I want to go back to anyway."

Amara looked. And for the first time she smiled. A sad smile — but real.

Chapter Four
ENCOUNTERS
Soyeon · Melina · Danjerino · Claudin & Claudyix

Every encounter is a contract. Unsigned, but binding.
— Eulogy

IV.I — Soyeon: The Time Reader

To find Soyeon, you first need to be silent. Truly silent — thoughts included. Because Soyeon reads time-light codes and this reading is affected by the noise around her.

Awamori didn't know this. She walked in. Soyeon didn't look at her.

Soyeon: "Empty your mind. Then speak."
Awamori: "How?"
Soyeon: "You need to learn how. I can't teach you. Eulogy can. But before Eulogy teaches you, I need to show you something."

Soyeon turned. Her eyes were open but her gaze was turned inward — not in this world, but in another.

Soyeon: "I see three possibilities for you. First: you find Awonade and everything changes. Second: you can't find it and Voidora expands. Third—"

Soyeon stopped. She stayed stopped for a long time.

Awamori: "What's the third?"
Soyeon: "Serendipity isn't showing me the third. That's either a very good or very bad thing."

'Very good or very bad' — both felt the same to Awamori. Excitement.

IV.II — Melina: The Cost of Light

Melina heals. This is a simple sentence but there's much behind it. Every healing pays a cost — where does this energy come from? From Euphoria. And does Euphoria deplete?

Awamori asked this. Melina laughed — a tired laugh.

Melina: "Euphoria doesn't deplete. But I can deplete. When I am the channel, my limit is the limit."
Awamori: "Isn't that dangerous?"
Melina: "Everything is dangerous. Even breathing — one day it will be the last breath."

Melina looked at Awamori. For a long time. Then she reached out her hand.

Melina: "There's something in you. Here—"

She pressed her finger to Awamori's chest. Awamori's breath caught — it wasn't physical. Deeper than that.

Melina: "There's an echo. An old echo. Someone — or something — you carry with you."
Awamori: "Who?"
Melina: "I don't know. But they're not happy. And they want to speak with you."

Awamori didn't sleep that night.

IV.III — Danjerino: Art Born of Chaos

The one thing worth knowing about Danjerino in advance: he never behaves the way you expect.

Awamori found him in a battlefield — in the ruins of Dragsimo. Danjerino was fighting three Voidora creatures alone. He looked like he was going to lose. Then he won. How? With a combination Awamori couldn't comprehend.

When the battle ended, Danjerino turned. A wide grin on his face.

Danjerino: "You watched! Beautiful, wasn't it? I'm like a work of art — different in every battle."
Awamori: "You almost died."
Danjerino: "'Almost' is a beautiful word. How many times in my life have I almost died? I didn't count. Counting isn't fun."

Awamori observed. Was this man dangerous? Yes. Trustworthy? Unclear. But he had one thing: he was genuine. Every move, every word, every absurd decision — genuine. Not calculated.

Awamori: "Why are you here?"
Danjerino: "Why not? Every corner of Dragsimo has a secret. I love secrets. Especially ones ready to explode."

IV.IV — Claudin and Claudyix: Two Voices in One Body

When Claudin speaks, logic speaks. When Claudyix speaks, intuition speaks. The same mouth, the same voice — but if you can listen, you understand the difference.

When Awamori first encountered them she didn't understand. In the middle of a sentence, the tone of voice changed. The eye color changed. The posture changed.

Claudin: "Let us explain our situation. I'm Claudin — logic and strategy. Claudyix is—"

The voice changed.

Claudyix: "—intuition and feeling. Hello. There's an old voice inside you. I can hear it."
Awamori: "Everyone says that."
Claudyix: "Because everyone is telling the truth."

The voice changed again.

Claudin: "Apologies. Claudyix sometimes ignores boundaries."
Claudyix: "No I don't, and I won't apologize."

Both voices spoke at the same time — for just a moment. Then silence. Awamori didn't know what to say. But she felt it mattered.

Chapter Five
DARKNESS
Shimorax · Shux · Ragna · Noravo

Darkness is not evil. Darkness is simply where light is absent. But Voidora is different — there, someone wants the light to be absent.
— Awamori — inner voice

V.I — Shimorax: General of the Void

Shimorax is a name. And in Voidora, a name is power — nameless beings dissolve. Shimorax doesn't dissolve. Not for centuries.

Awamori never saw him directly — no one does. But she saw his effects: the Lurkers in Dragsimo's ruins were under Shimorax's command. So were the Shadow Lurkers in Ashenveil. All feeding from the same source.

Why is Shimorax interested in Ashenveil? He has a connection to Voss — but which direction does that connection flow? Is Voss using Shimorax, or is Shimorax using Voss? Or are both unknowingly serving the same system?

The answer to this question is not given in this book. Because the answer is not yet known. Or someone knows but isn't saying.

V.II — Shux: The Thief Himself

Shux steals fragments of reality. This is not a metaphor — literally, physically, he takes something from one location and transfers it to another dimension. He is trying to steal the Crx key because Crx controls all inter-dimensional gateways.

Awamori encountered Shux for the first time in Supeytrenti — in the busiest market of the trading city. In the middle of the city, something disappeared. A small thing — a crystal on a stall. But the way it disappeared was strange: as if it had never been there.

Awamori: "You took it."

She looked around. Someone was listening — she could feel it. Awamori was tracking by sound vibration.

Shux: "Smart kid. Yes, I took it. Give me something and I'll give it back."
Awamori: "What for?"
Shux: "Are you genuinely curious? Or are you just asking to talk?"

Shux didn't appear. But his voice was there — coming from every direction. Awamori focused. She used the echoes. And for a moment she sensed: Shux's real location.

But at that moment Shux was gone. Truly gone — inter-dimensional, leaving no trace.

For the first time, Awamori sensed someone but couldn't catch them. This was both a disappointment and a lesson.

V.III — Ragna: The Last One Standing

To find Ragna you need to go to Walhalla. To go to Walhalla you don't need to be dead — but going in alive and coming out alive isn't easy either.

Awamori went in. She followed the route Eulogy had described. She walked among the ruins. Lost souls were there — but they didn't touch her. As if they knew. As if permission had been granted.

Ragna was sitting on a high stone. She wore armor — not dysfunctional, not decorative, just very tired. Her eyes were closed.

Ragna: "Awamori."
Awamori: "You know me?"
Ragna: "Not you. Your echo. An old echo — very old."

She opened her eyes. Her gaze was heavy — the weight of centuries.

Ragna: "I watched Walhalla's collapse. I watched how gods ended. And they ended because they were finished — truly finished. Power remained but will was gone."
Awamori: "Why are you telling me this?"
Ragna: "Because you may face the same danger. Finding Awonade strengthens you. But power consumes will. And when it's consumed — what remains?"

Awamori couldn't answer. Ragna didn't seem to be waiting either.

V.IV — Noravo: Three Times, One Consciousness

Noravo is not singular — there are three. The projections of the same consciousness at three different points in time. Past Noravo, present Noravo, future Noravo. All three exist simultaneously — but each knows different things.

Awamori saw all three. At the same time. This is normally impossible — but Awamori's echo perception can distinguish different time layers from each other.

Noravo (Past): "You came here before."
Noravo (Present): "You are coming now."
Noravo (Future): "And you will come again. But on your third visit, you will be someone different."

All three spoke simultaneously — the sound layered. Awamori felt dizzy.

Awamori: "Can you change fate?"
Noravo (All Three): "Who determines fate in the first place?"

No answer to this question exists. Or the answer was the question itself.

Chapter Six
AWONADE
The Chosen of Stars · Archives · Eclipse

Awonade is not a person. It is a form. And every form has its time.
— Archives — Final Record

VI.I — Entering Archives

Archives is everywhere and nowhere.

Eulogy had said this. Awamori had understood — theoretically. Understanding it in practice was different.

To enter Archives you first need complete silence. Then an echo — your own echo, the deepest, the oldest. And when you send that echo outward, the door opens.

Awamori tried. The first time the door didn't open — the echo wasn't deep enough. The second time the door opened but immediately closed. The third time Chico helped.

Chico: "You're sending your echo in the wrong direction. Not outward — inward."
Awamori: "What's the difference?"
Chico: "The difference is this: when you send it outward, Archives listens to you. When you send it inward, Archives recognizes you."

Awamori sent it inward. The door opened.

Archives was infinite — this is not figurative. It was truly infinite. Shelves in every direction. Records on every shelf. Each record with a weight — some from hundreds of years ago, some from yesterday.

And in a corner, Eulogy — as always, eyes closed, listening.

VI.II — The Record of Awonade

Eulogy brought Awamori to a record. Old — very old. Not paper, but crystal. Axios crystal. A voice echoed within it.

Awamori listened. And recognized.

That voice was her own voice. But deeper, older, more — complete. As if her current self was unfinished, and that voice was the whole.

Eulogy: "Awonade is a legendary form possessing the power to renew the universe. You are the modern version of this power. But you are not yet complete."
Awamori: "How do I become complete?"
Eulogy: "We wait for Eclipse. When Euphoria and Voidora energies overlap under Axios resonance — at that moment you can become complete. Or you can cease to exist."
Awamori: "What's the difference between the two?"
Eulogy: "You decide."

Silence. Inside Archives, silence was different — it was full. Every record was breathing, as it were.

Awamori: "And Voss? Does she have a connection to Awonade?"
Eulogy: "Voss wrote her first contract against Awonade's last form. That form was defeated. But it didn't disappear — it reincarnated. In you."

Awamori understood now. The name on her palm — that name wasn't hers. It was the name of Awonade's old form. And Voss was still looking for it.

VI.III — Eclipse Begins

It gave no warning. No Eclipse ever gives warning — Serendipity shifts one millimeter but doesn't tell you the time.

The sky changed. Euphoria's gold and Voidora's deep purple simultaneously — overlapping without destroying each other, together. Eclipse.

Awamori felt it. In her chest — exactly where Melina had placed her finger — a vibration. Not an echo this time. A voice. Clear, open, direct.

Awonade's voice.

And that voice said:

Are you ready? One chance. Decide before Eclipse ends. Either draw all echoes inside you and become Awonade — or let go, remain human. Both are valid. Both are real. But both cannot exist at the same time.

Awamori closed her eyes. Around her everyone had stopped — Eulogy, Chico, Soyeon, Melina, Danjerino, Claudin and Claudyix. All waiting.

Ragna's words echoed: 'Power consumes will. When it's consumed — what remains?'

Amara's words echoed: 'You say there's no place you want to go back to. But is there a place you want to go?'

And Maren's words — from hundreds of kilometers away, from Ashenveil — echoed: 'Sometimes waiting is also a skill.'

Awamori opened her eyes.

Awamori: "Both."

Eulogy was surprised. Eulogy showing surprise for the first time.

Eulogy: "What?"
Awamori: "You said both cannot exist at the same time. But while presenting me options, you hid the third. Remaining human while becoming Awonade. Taking power without losing will. Drawing all echoes inside while not losing myself."

Silence. Eclipse continued. The sky was still divided in two.

Eulogy: "This has never been attempted before."
Awamori: "I know. That's why I'm trying."

And Awamori drew inward. Everything. All echoes, all voices, all forgotten names. Eclipse's energy flowed. Euphoria and Voidora simultaneously. Axios trembled.

For a moment everything stopped.

Then it continued.

Awamori was standing. She hadn't changed — outwardly. But her eyes were different. Within them, something very small, very deep. A light.

Chico: "How do you feel?"

Awamori thought. She really thought.

Awamori: "Full. But in a good way."

Chapter Seven
THE CONVERGENCE
The True Prize · Voss's Plan · Lapis and Axios

The Convergence is not a competition. It is a trap. But even a trap can be made to serve your own purpose.
— Awamori

VII.I — The True Value of Lapis

The prize of The Convergence is Lapis Lazuli control. Everyone knows this. But why is Lapis so valuable? Because it is pure Axios concentration. And controlling Axios means controlling contracts.

Voss understood this long ago. She didn't establish The Convergence — but she enabled its expansion. Because the more factions compete for Lapis, the more contracts are written. And every contract feeds the system.

Awamori understood this from Soyeon's prophecy. And when she understood it, she stopped — right in the middle of the competition.

Awamori: "If we win, Voss grows stronger. If we lose, she grows stronger too. How?"
Soyeon: "Every hand that touches Lapis leaves a trace. Voss reads those traces."
Awamori: "Then instead of winning..."
Soyeon: "No one should win Lapis. Yes."

VII.II — Dragold and the First Alliance

Dragold doesn't like Awamori. But he respects her. This difference matters — love blinds, respect enables seeing.

Awamori went to Dragold. Alone, unarmed, in Sword of Dragon territory.

Dragold: "Brave or stupid. I still haven't figured out the difference."
Awamori: "Don't you want to win The Convergence?"
Dragold: "I do. The best should win — that's the belief."
Awamori: "But what if the best loses and a better outcome results?"

Dragold looked. For a long time.

Dragold: "Explain."

Awamori explained. The true value of Lapis, Voss's plan, what Eclipse was. Dragold listened. He listened without asking — this was rare for him.

Dragold: "If this is true — and I sense that it is — then to win we need to lose."
Awamori: "Yes."
Dragold: "No one has ever done this."
Awamori: "I know."

Dragold laughed. A real laugh — deep, slightly bitter, but real.

Dragold: "Alright. But you should know, I should have said this: I am your local rival. And on a global scale, for the first time, I'm teaming up with you. This is a historic moment."
Awamori: "I'm aware."
Dragold: "Stay aware. Because it won't happen again. Next time — rival."

And that day Shadow Garden and Sword of Dragon pointed in the same direction for the first time.

VII.III — Voss's Return

Voss appeared at Dragonspine. At an utterly unexpected moment — right in the middle of The Convergence's final stage.

Awamori sensed her first. An echo — but this time very clear, very close. Voss's presence pressed down like a weight.

Voss: "Awamori. At last."
Awamori: "You were looking for me."
Voss: "Not you. What's inside you. I've been looking for Awonade's last form for a very long time."

Awamori stopped. Behind her — Dragold, Serena, Vera, Mila, Elis, Mireya — all of them.

Awamori: "I know what you're looking for inside me. And I won't give it."
Voss: "A choice?"
Awamori: "A choice."

Voss looked. And for the first time — truly the first time — something changed in her face. The smile was still there. But it reached her eyes. Why did it reach them?

Because Voss had found something interesting. And for Voss, something interesting is rare.

Voss: "Good. Then let us talk."

EPILOGUE
Is everything over? No. Everything has begun. That is the difference.
— 0A3A4A

The Convergence ended. There was no winner — or everyone won. No one touched Lapis. Voss withdrew her contract ink. The system ran one turn empty.

Was this enough? No. But it was a beginning.

Awamori returned to Okinawa. Night had fallen. Echoes were there — but this time they were different. More ordered. Clearer. As if their sources were now known.

Chico was beside her. Its blue light flickering.

Chico: "I need to ask something."
Awamori: "Ask."
Chico: "Are you happy?"

Awamori wasn't expecting this. A drone hadn't asked her this before. She paused.

Awamori: "I said full. Still is. But yes. I think yes."

Chico's blue light burned a little brighter.

And far away — in Ashenveil — Maren was sitting in her garden. Two cups of tea. She was drinking both now.

And even farther away — deep in Archives — Eulogy felt a new record beginning. Awamori's voice. For the first time, her own voice.

— The End —
History of Ashenveil · Second Book: Garden of Shadows

Third Book: Gate of Voidora — coming soon.
